item.title: CVE-2026-100981 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.4 | NVIDIA OpenShell for Linux contains a vulnerability in its layer-7 REST proxy where a sandboxed actor could bypass the proxy's policy enforcement by sending a request whose body framing is interpreted differently by the proxy and the upstream server, allowing a second request to be smuggled past policy checks. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might lead to data tampering and information disclosure.

item.title: CVE-2026-122125 - NVD - CVSS: não informado

item.title: CVE-2026-120287 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing.
In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable.
This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.
